slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: How a managed Mac fleet actually works

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Most Mac problems in a business are not really Mac problems. They are the result of nobody managing the devices centrally.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: With Apple Business Manager and automated device enrolment, a Mac bought for a new starter can be shipped straight to them. It enrols itself the first time it is switched on, applies your settings, installs the apps they need and lands ready to work. Nobody has to sit and build it, and nobody has to post it to us first.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Configuration profiles let us set the things that matter once and have them hold across every device: full-disk encryption on, the firewall enabled, a sensible screen lock, and administrator rights given deliberately rather than by default. New Macs inherit the same standard automatically.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: macOS releases, browsers and business apps are kept current on a schedule instead of whenever someone gets round to clicking the prompt. When a device is lost, or someone leaves, it can be locked or wiped remotely and the licences reclaimed rather than quietly disappearing.
